blocks.text: Maple Ridge Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

Maple Ridge farms is a city-wide topic, not a place with a parcel list — what trades is whole fee-simple farm and rural parcels, in and out of the ALR, under the bylaw's A1, A2 and A3 agricultural zones, and band status (in or out of the ALR, farm class or not) is not confirmed per parcel until that parcel is checked on the ALC maps, on title and in its BC Assessment record. No named acreage subdivision, no named farm, no bare-land strata farm product and no presale acreage offering was verified on any source.

items.t: Parcel sizes / zones —: the agricultural zone minimum lot sizes are not verified.

ALR vs non-ALR split: The current (post-2011) ALR total is not verified. Whether a specific parcel is in the ALR must be confirmed for that parcel, in the ALC's maps and on title, before any subdivision, residence or value assumption is priced — that per-parcel check is the topic's central diligence step.
Hobby acreage vs working-farm ground —: Buyer demographics are not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: Water and septic: non-domestic groundwater use (irrigation) requires a water licence under the Water Sustainability Act before the water can lawfully be used; domestic groundwater use does not require authorization. Onsite sewage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation and only an Authorized Person (a Professional Engineer or a Registered Onsite Wastewater Practitioner) can design, install, repair, maintain or inspect a sewerage system.

Flood plain: the City's A1–A3 checklist records flood plain status, minimum basement elevation and geotechnical items for agricultural properties — ask those questions on any lowland parcel before subject removal. Parcel-level floodplain status and flood construction levels for any specific farm parcel: Not verified.
The farm belt is a minority of the city: Anyone quoting a current Maple Ridge ALR total from a newer source should be asked for that source: it is not verified.

The 500 m² cap comes with a fill cap buyers miss: A principal residence on ALR land built without an ALC application must be 500 m² or less in total floor area AND have no more than 1,000 m² of fill placed for its construction. On low, wet lowland ground the fill limit can bind before the floor-area limit does.
Thin rural rows are a warning, not a signal: A farm price built on a rural sub-area "trend" is built on almost no sales.

faq.q: What am I actually buying when I buy a "Maple Ridge farm"?

faq.a: The current total is not verified, and farm parcels sit in defined rural pockets, not a continuous belt.
faq.q: How much of Maple Ridge is actually farm-reserve land?

faq.a: Only with a water licence: under the Water Sustainability Act, groundwater used for non-domestic purposes such as irrigation requires a licence and payment of water fees and rentals before lawful use; domestic groundwater use does not require authorization. Confirm the licence position for the parcel before offering.
faq.q: Can I irrigate from a well on the parcel?

faq.a: Assume onsite sewage until proven otherwise: a building with indoor plumbing not connected to a community sewer must use an onsite system complying with the Sewerage System Regulation, designed / installed / inspected only by an Authorized Person. The City's own A1–A3 checklist also records flood plain status and geotechnical items for agricultural properties — run those checks on any lowland parcel.
